Genie Sim is a simulation framework developed by AgiBot. It provides developers with efficient data generation capabilities and evaluation benchmarks to accelerate the development of embodied AI. Genie Sim establishes a comprehensive closed loop process, including trajectory generation, model training, benchmark testing, and deployment verification. Users can use this efficient simulation toolchain to quickly validate algorithm performance and optimize models. Whether it is a simple grasping task or complex manipulation, Genie Sim offers a highly realistic simulation environment and precise evaluation metrics, helping developers efficiently develop and iterate robot technologies.
The Genie Sim Benchmark, as an open-source evaluation version of Genie Sim, aims to provide accurate performance testing and optimization support for embodied AI models.

#### [2.3.1 Docker container (recommended)](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/?id=_231-docker-container-recommended)

1. Develop using Docker containers
   - Install Docker according to the [ Isaac Sim documentation ](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/installation/install_container.html)
2. Prepare the Docker image

   ```bash

   ```

```Plain
# 进入 genie_sim 根目录并从 Dockerfile 创建 Docker 镜像docker build -f ./scripts/dockerfile -t registry.agibot.com/genie-sim/open_source:latest .
```

If you encounter network problems, my approach is:

```bash
ip addr show docker0 | grep "inet\s" | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d/ -f1DOCKER_HOST_IP="172.17.0.1" docker build \  --add-host=host.docker.internal:"$DOCKER_HOST_IP" \  --build-arg http_proxy="http://host.docker.internal:7890" \  --build-arg https_proxy="http://host.docker.internal:7890" \  --build-arg no_proxy="localhost,127.0.0.1" \  -f ./scripts/dockerfile \  -t registry.agibot.com/genie-sim/open_source:latest .
```

- Run the Docker container and start the server

#### [2.4.2 Baseline Evaluation Framework](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_242-benchmark-evaluation-framework)

Configuration

Evaluate the configuration using ADER (Action Domain Evaluation Rule).

**Example**

JSON

```Plain
{  "Acts": [    {      "ActionList": [        {          "ActionSetWaitAny": [            {              "Follow": "beverage_bottle_002|[0.2,0.2,0.2]|right"            },            {              "Timeout": 120            },            {              "Onfloor": "beverage_bottle_002|0.0"            }          ]        },        {          "ActionSetWaitAny": [            {              "PickUpOnGripper": "beverage_bottle_002|right"            },            {              "Timeout": 120            },            {              "Onfloor": "beverage_bottle_002|0.0"            }          ]        },        {          "ActionSetWaitAny": [            {              "Follow": "handbag_000|[0.4,0.4,0.4]|right"            },            {              "Timeout": 120            }          ]        },        {          "ActionSetWaitAny": [            {              "Inside": "beverage_bottle_002|handbag_000|1"            },            {              "StepOut": 1000            }          ]        }      ]    }  ],  "Init": [],  "Objects": [    {      "bottle": [        "beverage_bottle_002"      ],      "handbag": [        "handbag_000"      ]    }  ],  "Problem": "pack_in_the_supermarket"}
```

**Current evaluation capabilities**

<style> td {white-space:nowrap;border:0.5pt solid #dee0e3;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;vertical-align:middle;word-break:normal;word-wrap:normal;}</style>

|                   |                                                   |                  |                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Action             | Description                                                | Base Class       | Syntax                              |
| COMMON             |                                                   |                  |                                 |
| ActionList        | Queue action: Internal actions are executed in order.                | ActionBase       | "ActionList":[]                 |
| ActionSetWaitAny  | Conditional queue action: The action completes when any internal action finishes. | ActionBase       | "ActionSetWaitAny":[]           |
| ActionWaitForTime | Time-based wait action: Similar to sleep, but does not block the thread. | ActionBase       | "ActionWaitForTime": 3.0        |
| TimeOut            | Timeout verification action: Checks for a timeout occurrence.         | ActionCancelBase | "Timeout": 60                   |
| StepOut            | Step limit verification action: Checks if the step limit has been reached. | ActionCancelBase | "StepOut": 100                  |
| ActionSetWaitAll  | Exits when all conditions are met.                                 | ActionBase       | "ActionSetWaitAll":[]           |
| CUSTOM              |                                                   |                  |                                 |
| Ontop             | One object is above another.                                    | EvaluateAction   | "Ontop": "active_obj            |
| Inside            | One object is inside another.                                    | EvaluateAction   | "Inside": "active_obj           |
| PushPull          | Checks if the sliding joint of the joint object is within [min, max]; used to determine whether a drawer-like object is open or closed. | EvaluateAction   | "PushPull": "obj_id             |
| Follow            | Checks if the left/right gripper is following a specific object within the range [x, y, z] defined by the bounding box. | EvaluateAction   | "Follow": "obj_id               |
| PickUpOnGripper   | The gripper grabs an object.                                      | EvaluateAction   | "PickUpOnRightGripper": "object |
| OnShelf           | The object is within a specific area.                              | EvaluateAction   |                                 |
| Onfloor           | Checks if the specified object falls below the reference height ref_z; if so, exits. | ActionCancelBase | `"Inside": "obj_id              |
| Cover             | Object A covers Object B.                                         | EvaluateAction   | "Cover": "active_obj            |

**Evaluation output data structure**

JSON

```Plain
//输出[  {    "task_type": "benchmark",    "model_path": "",    "task_uid": "13513cf3-2d88-421e-b3e5-dc0998a60970",    "task_name": "genie_task_supermarket",    "stage": "",    "result": {      "code": -1,      "step": 0,      "msg": "",      "progress": [],      "scores":[]    },    "start_time": "2025-06-05 15:04:31",    "end_time": "2025-06-05 15:05:40"  }]
```

**Error Code**

Python

```Plain
from enum import Enumclass ErrorCode(Enum):    INIT_VALUE = -1    SUCCESS = 0    ABNORMAL_INTERRUPTION = 1    OUT_OF_MAX_STEP = 2    UNKNOWN_ERROR = 500
```

#### [2.5.2 Integrate one's own policy](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_252-integrate-your-own-policy)

1. Build your own code according to the following instructions.

2. a. Start model integration using the template on the following path. Do not modify the structure of the `infer` function.

```Plain
main├── model│   ├──demo_infer.py
```

b. When customizing, ensure that the ROS node strictly follows the specified topic.

*The communication between model inference and simulation environments is standardized and implemented based on ROS2. These are dedicated topics specified for tasks.

<style> td {white-space:nowrap;border:0.5pt solid #dee0e3;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;vertical-align:middle;word-break:normal;word-wrap:normal;}</style>

|                            |      |      |                 |                   |
| -------------------------- | ---- | ---- | --------------- | ----------------- |
| Topic Name                   | Publisher | Subscriber | Message Type     | Content               |
| /joint_command             | Model   | Simulation Environment | JointState    | Joint commands from model inference |
| /joint_states              | Simulation Environment | Model   | JointState    | Current robot joint state from simulation |
| /sim/head_img              | Simulation Environment | Model   | CompressedImage | Current head RGB image from simulation |
| /sim/left_wrist_img        | Simulation Environment | Model   | CompressedImage | Current left wrist RGB image from simulation |
| /sim/right_wrist_img       | Simulation Environment | Model   | CompressedImage | Current right wrist RGB image from simulation |
| /sim/head_depth_img        | Simulation Environment | Model   | CompressedImage | Depth image of the current head from simulation |
| /sim/left_wrist_depth_img  | Simulation Environment | Model   | CompressedImage | Depth image of the current left wrist from simulation |
| /sim/right_wrist_depth_img | Simulation Environment | Model   | CompressedImage | Depth image of the current right wrist from simulation |

c. After customization, ensure that the file structure matches the specified layout, and make sure it contains `infer.py` and `genie_sim_ros.py`.

```Plain
main├── AgiBot-World│   ├── scripts│   │   └── infer.py│   │   └── ...│   │   └── ...│   ├──genie_sim_ros.py│   ├──...│   └──...
```

2. Run the docker container

Bash

```Plain
# 需要将 ~/assets 更改为 GenieSimAssets 文件夹SIM_ASSETS=~/assets ./scripts/start_gui.sh
```

3. Run model inference

4. Execute the following command in the root directory of genie_sim outside the docker container:

```Plain
./scripts/autorun.sh {TASK_NAME} infer
```

4. Model inference dependencies

Common Python libraries are listed in the `requirements.txt` file of the Genie Sim Benchmark repository and are pre-installed in the docker image of our manipulation test server. If additional Python libraries are needed to run the policy, a `requirements.txt` file containing these libraries can be uploaded to the test server along with the model files.

## [3. Use Case ](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_3-use-cases)

### [3.1 How to run the simulation with a single line of code](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_31-how-to-run-simulation-with-just-one-line-of-code)

1. Run the Docker container

Bash

```Plain
SIM_ASSETS=~/17robo/GenieSimAssets ./scripts/start_gui.sh
```

2. Execute the shell script in the `genie_sim` root directory outside the docker container

3. a. Task execution layout

Bash

```Plain
./scripts/autorun.sh {TASK_NAME}
```

b. Run PICO remote manipulation

Bash

```Plain
./scripts/autorun.sh {TASK_NAME} pico {HOST_IP}
```

c. Run keyboard remote manipulation

Bash

```Plain
./scripts/autorun.sh {TASK_NAME} keyboard
```

d. Run scenario playback

Bash

```Plain
./scripts/autorun.sh {TASK_NAME} replay {STATE_FILE_PATH}
```

e. Run model inference

Bash

```Plain
./scripts/autorun.sh {TASK_NAME} infer
```

f. Run cleanup

Bash

```Plain
./scripts/autorun.sh clean
```

3. In the terminal, press `q` or `Q` to stop the task normally. The `autorun` script enables ros topic logging by default. If not needed, remove the relevant code in the `autorun` script and ensure the output folder is cleaned regularly. (What information is stored? Where is it saved?)

---

### [3.2 How to set up the baseline task file ](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_32-how-to-set-up-a-benchmark-task-file)

Each reference task file contains the following 6 key elements:

1. **task** contains a unique task name

2. **objects** includes various task objects:

   1. `extra_objects`: Non-interactive object

   2. `fix_objects`: Interactive objects with a fixed initial pose

   3. `task_related_objects`: Interactive objects with random initial poses

3. **recording_setting** specifies the camera perspective to be recorded.

4. **robot** includes the robot ID, robot configuration file, and initial pose of the robot base.

5. **scene** specifies a set of scene information:

   1. `scene_id`: The unique name of the scenario

   2. `function_space_objects`: Randomly generate the cube region of `task_related_objects`

   3. `scene_info_dir`: Path of the scene asset

   4. `scene_usd`: Path of the scenario usd file

6. **stages** includes several sub-stages designed for planning tasks

   1. `action`: Define the action name

   2. `active`: Define active objects, such as grippers

   3. `passive`: Defines passive objects, such as bottles

---

### [3.3 How to Create a Complete Benchmark Task with a Embodied AI Model](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_33-how-to-create-a-complete-benchmark-task-with-embodied-ai-model)

1. First, assemble the task template, such as "genie_task_supermarket.json". This configuration file contains details like robots, scenes, objects, and stages.

```Plain
benchmark/bddl/eval_tasks/your_task.json
```

Please fill in the asset file path correctly. The program will search for assets in the user-configured environment variable `SIM_ASSETS`.

2. Scenario generalization: Map tasks to scenarios

```Plain
文件路径: benchmark/bddl/task_to_preselected_scenes.json
```

JSON

```Plain
{  "genie_task_supermarket": [    "scenes/genie/supermarket_02/Collected_emptyScene_01/emptyScene_01.usd"  ]}
```

3. Write the evaluation standard code, for example

```Plain
文件路径: benchmark/bddl/task_definitions/genie_task_supermarket/problem0.bddl
```

Lisp

```Plain
(define (problem restock_shelves)    (:domain isaac)    (:objects        benchmark_beverage_bottle_013 - bottle.n.01    )    (:init        (onfloor benchmark_beverage_bottle_013 floor.n.01_2)    )    (:goal        (onshelf ?benchmark_beverage_bottle_013)    ))
```

Now, the baseline configuration steps are completed.

4. Access the embodied AI model in "yourpolicy.py". (Please refer to demopolicy.py)

Python

```Plain
class YourPolicy(BasePolicy):def __init__(self) -> None:super().__init__()        """初始化配置并加载模型。"""passdef reset(self):"""重置。"""passdef act(self, observations, **kwargs) -> np.ndarray:"""根据观察结果采取行动。        参数: observations 包含机器人图像 (Head_Camera_01/Right_Camera_01/Left_Camera_01) 和当前关节信息        返回: 机器人目标关节        """pass
```

5. Finally, run the client and evaluate your AI model.

Bash

```Plain
python3 benchmark/task_benchmark.py --task_name {task name} --policy_class {policy name} --env_class OmniEnv
```

### [3.4 Best Practices for Manipulation Task Asset Parameters](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_34-best-practice-of-asset-parameters-for-manipulation-task)

#### [3.4.1 How to debug colliders in IsaacSim](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_341-how-to-debug-collider-in-isaacsim)

> Enable the collision object debugging mode according to the instructions

---

#### [3.4.2 Bad Example](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_342-bad-examples)

- Complex grids can lead to collision calculation errors; the simpler, the better.

- Having too many triangular meshes in a small area usually leads to mesh collisions.

convexHull and convexDecompisition

---

#### [3.4.3 Good Example](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_343-good-examples)

Good means easy to grasp and minimal grid collisions

- A good collision mesh usually looks simple and clean.

- Ensure that the grasping of key areas is precise (such as cans, bottles, and caps)

ConvexDecompisition grid

convexDecompisition collision body

convexHull

## [4. API Reference ](https://agibot-world.com/sim-evaluation/docs/#/v2?id=_4-api-reference)

<style> td {white-space:nowrap;border:0.5pt solid #dee0e3;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;vertical-align:middle;word-break:normal;word-wrap:normal;}</style>

|                                 |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| Function                          | Description             | Input                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Output                                                                                                                                    |
| Initialization                      |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.InitRobot()                 | Initialize robot and scene | robot_cfg: Path to configuration file (located in 'robot_cfg' folder)<br>scene_usd: USD path<br>init_position([x,y,z])<br>init_rotation([x,y,z])                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| Controller                            |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.moveto()                        | The end effector of the robot moves to the target pose      | target_position([x,y,z])<br>target_quaternion([w,x,y,z])<br>is_backend:<br>1. True: ee linear movement<br>2. False: ee obstacle avoidance movement<br>ee_interpolation:<br>1. True: ruckig interpolation<br>2. False: target point interpolation<br>distance_frame: interpolation density                                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.set_joint_positions()          | The robot's joints move to the target joint state       | target_joint_position: [N], rad/s<br>joint_indices: [N], index<br>is_trajectory:<br>1. True: joint action application<br>2. False: set joint state                                                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.set_gripper_state()            | Set gripper state (open or closed)         | gripper_command: "open" or "close"<br>is_right(bool)<br>opened_width(float)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.SetTrajectoryList()            | Set ee pose list trajectory              | trajectory_list(list): [[position(xyz), rotation(wxyz)]]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                       |
| Object                           |                                                                                              |                                                                                                                                              |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.add_object()               | Add a USD object to the scene        | usd_path(str): Relative path of the asset based on SIM_ASSETS <br>prim_path(str): Prim path of the object in the scene, e.g.: "/World/Object/obj_01" <br>lable_name(str): Name of the object label applied for semantic segmentation <br>target_position([x,y,z]) <br>target_quaternion([w,x,y,z]) <br>target_scale([x,y,z]) <br>mass: [kg] <br>**add_particle(bool): Add additional fluid particles, e.g.: water in a kettle <br>particle_size: ([x,y,z]) <br>particle_position: ([x,y,z]) |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.SetMaterial()              | Set the material for XFormPrim      | material_info(list): <br> e.g.: <br>material_info = [<br>{"object_prim" : "/obj1" <br>"material_name": "wood" <br>"material_path: "materials/wood"}]                                                                                                                                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.SetLight()                | Set the lighting information of the stage | light_info(list): <br> e.g.: <br>light_info = [{<br>"light_type": "Distant", <br>"light_prim": "/World/DistantLight", <br>"light_temperature": 2000, <br>"light_intensity": 1000, <br>"rotation": [1,0.5,0.5,0.5], <br>"texture": ""}]                                                                                                                  |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.SetObjectPose()           | Set the pose of rigid bodies and joint objects in a single physics step | object_info(list): <br> e.g.: <br>object_info = [{<br>"prim_path": "/World/obj1", <br>"position": [x,y,z], <br>"rotation": [w,x,y,z]}]<br>object_joint_info(list): Joint information of joint objects                                                                                                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                       |
| Sensor                             |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.AddCamera()              | Add a camera to the stage        | camera_prim(str): Prim path of the camera <br>camera_position(xyz): Position of the camera <br>camera_rotation(wxyz): Rotation of the camera <br>Width, Height, focus_length, horizontal_aperture<br>vertical_aperture Internal parameters of the camera:<br>fx = Width * focus_length / horizontal_aperture<br>fy = Height * focus_length / vertical_aperture<br>is_local(bool): Local or world pose                                |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.capture_frame()          | Capture rgb/depth frames        | camera_prim(str): Prim path of the camera                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | response.color_image.data<br>response.depth_image.data                                                                                |
| client.capture_semantic_frame() | Capture semantic frames          | camera_prim_path(str): Prim path of the camera                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | response.semantic_mask.data                                                                                                           |
| Observation                         |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.get_observation()        | Obtain camera/joint/tf data in a single frame     | data_keys(dict):<br> For example:<br>data_keys = { 'camera': {<br>'camera_prim_list': ["/camera"],<br>'render_depth': True,<br>'render_semantic': True<br>},<br>'pose': ["/object1" ],<br>'joint_position': True,<br>'gripper': True}                                                                                                                   | observation = {<br>"camera": camera_datas,<br>"joint": joint_datas,<br>"pose": object_datas,<br>"gripper": gripper_datas }            |
| client.GetIKStatus()            | Inverse kinematics calculation                | target_poses(list): [{"position":xyz, "rotation":wxyz}]<br>is_right(bool): Arm type for both arms<br>ObsAvoid(bool): IK with obstacle avoidance                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | "status"([bool]): Inverse kinematics successful<br>"Jacobian"([double]): Jacobian score of ik joint state<br>"joint_positions"([list]): Ik joint positions<br>"joint_names"([list]): Ik joint names |
| client.GetEEPose()              | Obtain world pose of end effector             | is_right(bool): Select arm type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | state.ee_pose.position<br>state.ee_pose.rpy                                                                                           |
| client.get_object_pose()        | Obtain world pose of object                | prim_path(str): Object prim path                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | object_pose.position<br>object_pose.rpy                                                                                               |
| client.get_joint_positions()    | Obtain current joint positions of robot      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | result.states.name<br>result.states.position                                                                                          |
| Curobo Feature Functions                |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.AttachObj()                    | Attach object to be attached    | prim_paths[list[str]]: Prim path of the attached object                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.DetachObj()                    | Separate all objects            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| Recording Settings                     |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.start_recording()              | Start recording segment         | data_keys(dict): Recording settings <br> For example: <br> data_keys = {<br>'camera': {<br>'camera_prim_list': [<br>'/World/base_link/Head_Camera'<br>],<br>'render_depth': True,<br>'render_semantic': True<br>},<br>'pose': [<br>'/World/obj1'<br>],<br>'joint_position': True,<br>'gripper': True<br>}<br>fps(int): Recording frame rate <br>task_name(str)                            |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.stop_recording()         | Stop recording              |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.reset()                  | Reset scene, robot, and object |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
| client.Exit()                   | Exit the application         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                       |
